title: August 2026 consumer prices rose with a gasoline-led energy contribution
source_unit: Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), U.S. city average
geography: United States city-average CPI-U; selected expenditure categories and national index aggregates

denominator.unit: CPI-U U.S. city-average price index built from BLS price quotations and expenditure weights; release does not disclose a respondent or quotation-count denominator

all_items.unit: percent seasonally adjusted change from July 2026

core.unit: percent seasonally adjusted change in all items less food and energy

observations.method: BLS CPI-U monthly index and percent-change release; seasonally adjusted monthly changes are compared with the prior month.
observations.uncertainty: The CPI is a price index, not a household-cost or welfare estimate. It uses an urban consumer expenditure framework, category weights, and sampled prices; the release's aggregate rates do not disclose household-level exposure or design-based uncertainty for a particular subgroup.
observations.subgroup: All urban consumers nationally; this observation is not a household, income-group, race/ethnicity, tenure, or rural/urban estimate.
observations.counterinterpretation: A monthly index increase does not show that every household paid more, reduced quantities, substituted, borrowed, or lost financial room. Composition, timing, quality change, location, and household-specific baskets can produce different lived inflation.

denominator.unit: CPI-U U.S. city-average price index; release does not disclose a respondent or quotation-count denominator

all_items.unit: percent unadjusted change over 12 months ending August 2026

core.unit: percent unadjusted change over 12 months ending August 2026

food.unit: percent unadjusted change over 12 months ending August 2026

energy.unit: percent unadjusted change over 12 months ending August 2026

shelter.unit: percent unadjusted change over 12 months ending August 2026

observations.method: BLS CPI-U twelve-month percent changes from the unadjusted index; category rates are not a household-specific budget decomposition.
observations.uncertainty: Twelve-month rates combine monthly index movements and retain the CPI's urban population, weighting, sampling, and quality-adjustment boundaries. They do not measure real income, liquid assets, debt service, or affordability by household.
observations.subgroup: All urban consumers nationally and major CPI expenditure categories.
observations.counterinterpretation: The high energy rate is not evidence that energy was the dominant burden for every household; exposure depends on vehicle use, home energy, commuting, housing arrangements, contracts, and ability to substitute.

observations.period: August 2026 gasoline and shelter monthly movements

denominator.unit: CPI-U U.S. city-average gasoline and shelter indexes; release does not disclose a household denominator

energy_contribution.value: over one third of the monthly all-items increase

observations.method: BLS release decomposition of selected CPI-U expenditure categories and their contribution to the aggregate monthly movement.
observations.uncertainty: Contribution statements describe index arithmetic, not incidence. They do not identify which households experienced gasoline, shelter, or food-away-from-home changes, nor whether costs were passed through to wages, margins, debt, or public assistance.
observations.subgroup: Selected CPI-U expenditure categories; no household subgroup estimate.
observations.counterinterpretation: A gasoline-led aggregate movement can coexist with different regional prices, commuting needs, vehicle efficiency, housing contracts, and income buffers; the CPI category is not a direct measure of hardship or political reaction.

boundary: This record adds an official August 2026 CPI-U price-index checkpoint to the household-pressure atlas. It does not establish household-specific inflation, affordability, consumption response, debt or saving change, trust, political action, or a causal link from gasoline, shelter, or food prices to cultural or geopolitical outcomes. The extracted retrieval hash is for the committed release-fact summary; the official release URL remains the authoritative source.
